Nice One vs Faces: two Gulf online beauty stores compared

Two regional multi-brand beauty destinations with heavy overlap. We compared them on range, price, delivery and which to check first.

Last updated: 15 August 2026

Nice One and Faces are two of the Gulf's biggest online beauty stores, both multi-brand, both carrying makeup, skincare and fragrance, both delivering fast across the region. Their catalogues overlap heavily on the mainstream names, so like the perfume houses, they are best treated as a pair to compare on a given product rather than a loyalty to pick, and a shopper who checks both rarely overpays on a shared brand.

The practical upshot is the same as with any closely matched pair: do not pledge loyalty to one, keep both and compare on the product in front of you. Because their mainstream catalogues overlap and their delivery and returns are both strong, the deciding factor on most orders is simply which is promoting harder on your brand this week — a two-minute check that routinely beats buying on habit. This guide covers where each leads, how buying beauty online works without in-store testing, and how to time the biggest savings.

There is a broader point worth holding onto: in a market this competitive, no single beauty store stays the cheapest for long, because a strong promotion from one pulls a matching response from the other within weeks. That churn is good for you, but only if you shop it — loyalty to a single app is precisely what lets you miss the better offer next door. So the whole strategy reduces to a habit rather than a preference: two tabs open, the same product in each, and the order placed wherever the final price after code and card is lower today, whichever store that turns out to be.

Overlap, price and delivery

Because both carry the mainstream makeup, skincare and fragrance a Gulf shopper wants, the deciding factor on a shared product is usually the live promotion: one will be running a stronger code, a gift-with-purchase or a bundle while the other is quiet. Both back authenticity and both deliver fast with easy returns, so the experience is close, and the win rotates week to week with whoever is promoting harder on the brand you are buying.

The differences show on the tails and the emphasis: one may stock a specific niche brand or shade the other skips, and each weights its range and its seasonal campaigns slightly differently. For a hard-to-find product, search both because stock differs; for a mainstream one, buy from whichever runs the better code that week. Neither is a permanent winner, which is exactly why comparing them is the value, and both go deepest at Eid when beauty gifting peaks.

The verdict

Treat Nice One and Faces as a pair to compare, not a loyalty to pick. For any mainstream beauty product, check the live code on both store pages and buy from whichever is stronger that week; for a niche or hard-to-find item, search both because stock differs on the tails. Time a bigger beauty purchase to Eid, when both run their deepest codes, and let the two compete for it. Both carry live codes on our store pages.

When the biggest beauty discounts land, and how to save

Both run their deepest codes, bundles and gift-with-purchase offers around the two Eids and the major seasonal events, when beauty gifting peaks, with steady promotions in between. For a planned restock of a staple — a foundation you always use, a skincare refill — timing it to one of these windows is the reliable saving. For an everyday order, the standing code plus a card offer is still worth stacking, because in beauty the small percentages add up across a routine you repurchase constantly.

The stack is standard: apply the store code first, confirm the drop, then pay with a bank card carrying a live offer, and split a bigger basket only if it helps. Our store pages for Nice One and Faces carry the currently-working code. Because the win rotates week to week, the habit that saves the most is the simplest one — check both pages, take the stronger code, add your card — rather than defaulting to whichever you used last time.

Buying beauty online: shades, samples and returns

The real risk in online beauty is not price but getting the wrong shade or formula, since you cannot swatch before you buy. Both stores help in different ways — detailed product info, shade descriptions, reviews and, on some lines, sample or mini sizes — but the smart approach is to buy the exact shade you already know online, and to use in-store testers or minis when trying something new. For a proven repurchase, online is pure convenience and saving; for a first-time shade, reduce the gamble before committing to a full size.

Returns matter more in beauty than most categories, because a mismatch is common and hygiene rules can limit what is returnable once opened. Both operate regional logistics with workable returns, so check each store's policy on opened cosmetics before you order something you are unsure about. Reserve the untested, easily-wrong purchases for whichever store makes returns simplest, and keep the confident repurchases for whoever has the better live code — that split protects both your money and your routine.

Quick answers

Which is cheaper? Neither consistently — compare both on the product before buying. Do they carry the same brands? Heavily overlapping on the mainstream; stock differs on niche lines, so search both for hard-to-find items. Are returns easy? Both run regional logistics; check each policy on opened cosmetics. When are the best deals? Around the two Eids and seasonal events, with steady codes in between. Check the live code on both store pages here and buy from whichever is stronger this week.
